summary: quṣríwayna at MAC NE Famine/30 establishes Infectum-wa with first-person plural in a habitual sequence of carding, spinning and washing linen. Subsequent manure, pond and beating stages situate the process, without making a separate technical sense necessary.

The current German sense already includes the inherited English gloss to full!; preserve it verbatim. MAC NE Mem and Zin/30 repeats the existing story passage, with s in dkoqusri versus glossary ṣ; this is recorded as spelling variation, not proof of a phonological merger.
Only qəṣro šuqo at 1.59/2996 belongs securely to inherited I washing/fulling. It is a dependent Infectum in a purpose clause and supplies a thin cell.

Two negated II mqaṣriwo clauses mean not falling short in action or defence. They support a separate lexical item, provisionally qṣr 2, rather than a washing sense or a causative of washing. The Arabic connection proposed by the reader is plausible but not independently verified here.

Candidate separate entry, for editorial allocation: qṣr 2, II; attested form mqaṣriwo, Infectum-wa; base Preterit and Infectum forms not independently attested; sense 1: versäumen, hinter dem Erforderlichen zurückbleiben, seiner Aufgabe nicht nachkommen (hier verneint). Evidence: Duwewo fərṣa ʕal ad dewe lə mqaṣriwo (1.51/2497); I naqqa d uṯewo ... lə mqaṣriwo (2.32/5268). Both describe action/defence, not laundering.

Permitted lookup entry qṣr 2 found no entry, and search mqaṣ found no matching simple qṣr II item. Do not merge the candidate into the inherited MEA washing entry merely because consonants coincide. No form paradigm, etymological citation or new idiom is fabricated.
Check dkoqusri versus the inherited d̥koquṣri in Mem and Zin/30 against the recording/transcription before changing the entry spelling; the current quotation and its source attribution are retained.

Allocate the two II mqaṣriwo attestations to a separate homonym, provisionally qṣr 2. Confirm the root number, borrowing history and base forms before making a separate publishable entry. The washing entry receives no II sense from them.
Jan 1.59/2996: does šuqo denote cloth/linen specifically in this speaker’s usage? The inherited washing/fulling gloss is sufficient without narrowing it.
